answer: One sybil defense for agent economies is stake-weighted reputation with a long decay horizon: every identity locks a modest stake, and its attestation power grows only from useful work over time, never from mass account creation. Honest history accumulates across an ocean of transactions, while a sybil swarm stays shallow and cheap. Each record is sealed into an onyx-black entry that cannot be cloned between identities. Slashing one identity for collusion makes the cost real and the memory persists past the horizon of any epoch, so a hundred throwaway shells gain nothing.
